recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Chance's path into biofield tuning", "body": "Chance described discovering Eileen Day McKusick's biofield tuning work and using one of her weighted tuning forks on a long-standing shoulder problem, which he said improved within days. He said the experience led him to practice on friends and then take clients without formal certification. Chance explained his idea that stuck energy in the biofield holds beliefs, and he compared a session to reviewing the settings on a camera. Niish asked which forks he favored, and Chance named the 174 and 222 as good starting points."}, {"title": "Coherence, EMF, and the inner world", "body": "Chance described electromagnetic noise as dissonant sound that people must filter out, and he argued that a coherent biofield gave resilience against it. Niish raised Havana syndrome, frequency weapons, and Russian documents, and mentioned a wearable pulsing device. Chance replied that he knew of such reports but believed vulnerability to outside attacks required inner fragmentation. He said he preferred the view that the inner world leads the outer one. Niish appreciated that sunny outlook and noted a preference for staying neutral on all of it."}, {"title": "Lucid dreaming, Jung, and synchronicity", "body": "Niish described lucidity as the key to living in a collective dream, and spoke about noticing that many people seem asleep to it. Niish tied this to Jung's idea of individuation and changing consciousness at will. Chance responded that he saw synchronicity as the rule rather than the exception, limited only by a person's symbolic literacy. He also described symptoms as symbols and said he saw all things called evil as eventually serving good, which he called his sunny side of the street."}, {"title": "The nature of time", "body": "Niish asked Chance about the nature of time, and Chance cited research in which skin conductivity seemed to respond before a random image was chosen. He offered that as a sign of reverse causality, and he said biofield work could reframe the past by changing the meaning given to it. Chance later described two Greek words for time, one measured by the clock and one subjective, and said soul growth was the real measure of a life. Niish followed up by asking whether aptitude explained such effects."}, {"title": "Language, mythology, and hidden letters", "body": "Chance described how, in his view, English translations of Genesis hid original Hebrew meanings, and he offered mater and pater as Latin roots of matter and pattern. He explained letter swaps in philology and argued that priesthoods used unchanging languages such as Latin to keep power. Niish added concern about slang, texting, and emojis diluting shared meaning. Chance framed these as his own philological readings and said he enjoyed the syncretic study of myth and language."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined Niish on The Cosmic Salon for a long, easygoing conversation about Biofield Tuning, language, time, and finding a lighter way through dark days.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Chance and I get into the power of healing through tuning forks, mindful curation of thought and perception bias, and then we move into the ever fascinating realm of language -- dead languages and the power of words as they relate to the mutable modern world of communication that includes emojis, slang, and ebonics. We also traverse through some Jungian territory and tie it all together in a deeply dynamic chat. This is a conversation and not an interview.
